items.title: Ava: a real-time talking avatar that runs fully in the browser on WebGPU
items.summary: Hugging Face's Victor Mustar shows Ava, a voice-chat avatar where speech understanding, the reply and the animated head all run on the user's device in the browser. It chains Liquid's LFM3-Omni with Hugging Face's WebGPU kernels and the TalkingHead and HeadAudio libraries, and a live Space is public. The author calls it a tech demo; the model download is about 1.6 GB.

doubt.pushback: Author labels it a tech demo. Replies raise WebGPU support on older laptops and the 1.6 GB first load, and one user found the voice quality rough.

items.reception: Mostly impressed by the fully local setup; the practical concerns are hardware support and download size.

items.title: Meituan releases LongCat-2.5, a 1.6T-parameter multimodal agent model, API only
items.summary: Meituan's LongCat-2.5 is a natively multimodal mixture-of-experts model with about 1.6T total and roughly 48B active parameters, aimed at agent work. Meituan's blog reports Terminal Bench v2.1 88.4, BrowseComp 91.9 and MCP Atlas 83.1, and says W4A4 inference gives about 43% faster prefill and 42.8% faster decode than W8A8. It is available through an API at a limited-time price of $0.30 in and $1.20 out per million tokens; no weights were released.

doubt.pushback: All benchmark numbers are Meituan's own; API only, no weights, so nothing is independently checked yet.

items.title: DeepMind researchers use Antigravity with UI sidecars to screen proteins and draft a wet-lab plan
items.summary: Google shows DeepMind researchers working in Antigravity to search millions of uncharacterized proteins, validate a new antimicrobial peptide and produce a wet-lab experiment plan. The workflow leans on Antigravity UI sidecars, custom viewers the agent builds next to the chat so researchers can inspect protein structures directly. DeepMind's blog post has the full write-up.

doubt.pushback: Vendor showcase. Replies note the plan still has to survive real lab work and that instrument and reagent queues dominate the timeline.

items.reception: Replies single out the sidecar viewer as the useful part; skepticism is about the lab step, not the tool.

items.title: levelsio: Claude Code edited a full 10-minute vlog from raw clips on a MacBook
items.summary: Pieter Levels asked Claude Code (Opus 5.5) to cut his DJI clips into a 10-minute vlog. Unprompted, it transcribed audio locally with mlx-whisper (Whisper large-v3-turbo on Apple MLX), built frame contact sheets so it could see each clip, used SpeechBrain ECAPA to tell his voice from others, made thumbnails with OpenCV and YuNet face detection, wrote the edit as a JSON cut list, and burned in captions with Pillow. He made only small fixes.

doubt.pushback: Single first-hand report; no code or prompt shared.

items.title: SemiAnalysis: NVIDIA AgentX submission reports over 1,000 tokens/s per user on 700B+ models
items.summary: SemiAnalysis reports a new NVIDIA entry in its AgentX inference benchmark where agent-swarm-written kernels push HBM GPUs past 1,000 tokens per second per user on 700B+ parameter models. It also cites 20.9 times better performance per total cost of ownership on Rubin NVL72 than GB300 NVL72 at 325 tokens per second per user.

doubt.pushback: Vendor submission relayed by SemiAnalysis; the post links no submission details, and the Rubin figure is a projection on unreleased hardware.
